title: Statistics & Inference
subtitle: Foundations first, then the core of MacKay's Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms. Short sessions, unlimited practice, spaced repetition.

lectures.title: Information Theory, Pattern Recognition and Neural Networks (16 lectures, Cambridge, 2012)
lectures.note: Titles of lectures 2-5, 7 and 8 follow the 2012 slide list; the others follow the course and video pages.

list.title: Entropy and data compression (I): introduction to compression, information content
Entropy and data compression (II): source coding theorem, the bent coin lottery
Entropy and data compression (III): symbol codes
Entropy and data compression (IV): arithmetic coding
Noisy channel coding (I): inference and information measures for noisy channels
Noisy channel coding (II): the capacity of a noisy channel
Noisy channel coding (III): the noisy-channel coding theorem
A noisy channel coding gem, and an introduction to Bayesian inference (I)
An introduction to Bayesian inference (II): inference of parameters and models
Approximating probability distributions (I): clustering as an example inference problem
Approximating probability distributions (II): Monte Carlo methods (I): importance sampling, rejection sampling, Gibbs sampling, Metropolis method
Approximating probability distributions (III): Monte Carlo methods (II): slice sampling, hybrid Monte Carlo, over-relaxation, exact sampling
Data modelling with neural networks (I): feedforward networks
Data modelling with neural networks (II): content-addressable memories and state-of-the-art error-correcting codes

parts.title: Part A · Foundations
parts.description: Probability and classical statistics the book assumes, plus the frequentist methods it argues with.

parts.title: Part B · Information, inference and learning (MacKay)
parts.description: Core of ITILA: entropy, Bayesian inference, model comparison, maximum likelihood, Monte Carlo, and Bayes vs sampling theory.
